holiday.title: International Thank You Day
holiday.description:
On this day, many countries around the world celebrate the International Thank You Day, created by the UN and UNESCO. As part of the holiday, events, exhibitions, open lessons are held to remind people of courtesy and gratitude.

Gratitude is one of the most powerful, magical feelings that make us happy. It acts through the main law of the Universe: what we radiate is what we receive in response. Using words and thoughts of gratitude, we share positive energy, which returns back to us rewarding with the fulfillment of our desires, success, income and well-being.

The path to the opening of the soul and heart, the purification of karma begins with the ability to be grateful and thankful for what you have. This positively affects our relationships with loved ones, colleagues and ourselves and also directs thinking in a positive direction.

Learning the art of gratitude is easy. Before going to bed, say to yourself why you are grateful and to whom. This will help you to wake up every morning with a feeling of joy and lightness. It is also helpful to keep Gratitude Diary daily. The most important thing is to write down even little things for which you are thankful today. And then you will begin to notice what makes every moment of your life so special and unique, allowing you to love it more and more.

holiday.title: Lohri
holiday.description:
The Lohri holiday is celebrated annually on January 13 in Punjab (North India). Thousands of bonfires are lit on this day. They symbolize the end of a harsh winter. Bonfire is a personification of Agni — the Indian god of fire. 

A ritual circumambulation around the fire is called "parikrama". People go around the fire in clockwise direction reading prayers with requests for well-being. After completing the parikrama, they make "prasad" — the distribution of food offered to the deity and then given to the faithful as a spiritual and sacred gift, as a symbol of divine grace.

The Lohri holiday is celebrated by observing fasting and presenting gifts to each other in the family. In the late evening, a lavish feast is held, as the last chance to enjoy animal food before fasting. During the night, people have fun around the fire, dancing and singing songs. In the morning, children start going to neighboring houses and "caroling", singing songs and demanding "ransom" for this. This rite is called Dulha Bhatti.

Some of the treats brought by children are thrown into the fire. It means burning the old and starting the New Year.

The day following Lohri is called Maghi, it marks the arrival of the month of Magha. On this day, it is important to take a bath in The Ganges River. Women prepare treats: usually sweet rice and crystal sugar.

Another interesting tradition of the festival is the performance of the traditional Punjabi dance Bhangra. Only men are allowed to perform it.

Lohri is a warm family holiday, it is better to spend it with loved ones. Clean up the house, light candles — they will clear the space of negative energy. Prepare festive dishes and treat your neighbors.

holiday.title: Pongal
holiday.description:
Pongal is a traditional South Indian festival celebrating prosperity, wellness and good harvest. It is one of the most important festivals in the Hindu calendar year. It is celebrated in January, after the winter solstice.

The date of the holiday was determined according to the solar calendar and it doesn’t change, taking place on the 14th of January. According to the Hindu calendar, the New Year begins with a Pongal holiday.

It is believed that the holiday marks the end of the unfavorable phase and the beginning of a new chapter in life. Any favorable and sacramental rituals may be performed in every house on this day. From a scientific point of view, the winter transits into the spring at that time.

Like many traditional holidays, Pongal is surrounded by legends, one of the most popular is the legend of God Shiva and his bull Nandi. The god sent his sacred bull Nandi to the people so that he would order them to take an oil bath daily and to eat once a month. But Nandi mixed everything up and told people to wash once a month and to eat every day. Then Shiva sent him to the Earth to help people with the harvest. This is how Pongal became the Harvest Festival.

The holiday is celebrated for four days; each day symbolizes an important phase.

The first day of the holiday is called Bhogi Pongal. Bonfires are burned on that day and unnecessary household items are thrown into them to burn. Girls sing and perform traditional dances. At the same time, the preparations for the second day of the festival take place at everyone’s homes: rice, sugarcane and turmeric are being prepared for the rituals.

The second (main) day is called Surya Pongal and is dedicated to the Hindu god of the Sun. The day starts with an act of worship called Puja. Rice should be boiled in a pot for that ceremony and should be mixed with the turmeric the day before. This rice is offered to the god Surya. Also, there are such traditional offerings as coconuts, bananas and sugarcane. People dress up in festive outfits and paint sacred signs on their bodies. They depict the face of the god on the wooden boards called Kolams, using colored rice flour.

The third day of the festival is called Mattu Pongal and on this day the cows are worshipped. Cows are washed, painted and decorated with beads, garlands and bells. Bedizened animals are brought into the city where the festival continues with their participation in it. The treats which were offered to the gods are now offered to the cows.

The fourth (final) day is called Kaanum Pongal. Celebrations end surrounded by one's family and relatives give each other gifts, dance and pray for a prosperous life.

The festival is not only the beginning of the harvest season but also a traditional wedding month.

During the days of the celebration of Pongal, it is best to gather as a family, as well as to prepare different dishes made from rice. Share treats with neighbors and relatives, as this symbolizes abundance. Remember, that abundance, prosperity and light come only into clean houses and bodies. Get rid of old things, free space for new ones.

holiday.title: International hug day
holiday.description:

Hugs are a symbol of intimacy and love. They give a sense of security, calmness, harmonize our nervous system, stimulate the production of hormones of joy and generally strengthen the immune system. With hugs, we teach children to love others, give support and understanding to adults, and remind the elderly that they are not alone. With more hugs in our life, we become happier and stronger psychologically.

On this day various campaigns and flash mobs are being held in many countries. People take to the streets and embrace each other, thus showing goodwill and the desire for world peace.

Hug day helps us to remember that we are all one, that we feel and think alike. This is a chance for us to share a bit of warmth even with strangers. But the most important thing on this day — engage in a long, strong embrace with your closed ones, tell them how much you love them and feel that magical power of touch.

holiday.title: Ganesha’s birthday
holiday.description:
Ganesha is one of the most beloved and revered gods. His birthday, Ganesha Chaturthi, is a very anticipated and auspicious day. The holiday has no exact date; it is celebrated in the month of Bhadra (August – September).

Ganesha is a God of wisdom and prosperity. His other name is Ganapati. He is the son of God Shiva and his wife Parvati. There are several legends about his birth. According to the most popular one, Parvati thought so lovingly when thinking about her husband Shiva while bathing in the sacred lake that she entered a deep meditative state. In this condition, she gave birth to a divine child. He immediately turned into a young man, handsome in appearance and bright-minded.

Parvati asked her son not to let anyone closer while she was engaged in her bathing rituals. Ganesha stood guard over his mother when Shiva returned. He saw a strange man near his wife and instantly chopped off his head.

Parvati’s grief was terrible. Seeing the despair of his wife and hearing the whole essence of the situation, Shiva commanded to bring the head of the first living creature and put it on the body of his son. The creature turned out to be the elephant Airavata. So the elephant-headed god of wisdom and prosperity appeared to the world.

According to Vedic tradition, Ganesha represents the mantra “Om” with which any ceremony begins.

The purity of body, space and thoughts will help you to build the right relationship with the god of wisdom and prosperity. 

Start your day before sunrise. The birth of Ganesha and holiday rituals are closely related to water, so bathing in a pond or taking a bath after waking up is an important part of the day. Keep fast all day. Refuse stodgy foods, replace it with fruits and fresh juices. But don’t refuse treats for the divine guest. Ganesha is fond of sweets, especially nuts and coconut balls with a sweet core, as well as fresh and dried fruits. Decorate your home with flowers and red fabrics, light incense and devote time to reading mantras.

OM GAM GANAPATAYE NAMAHA is one of the most famous mantras. It carries the strength that will help in overcoming obstacles, bestow purity of thoughts and fill life with prosperity and galore. 

Don’t be selfish. Your intentions should be pure and sincere and your thoughts should be bright. Only then Ganesha will hear you and help to remove all obstacles on the righteous path.

holiday.title: Saraswati
holiday.description:
This bright holiday glorifies Saraswati — the goddess of knowledge and education. Goddess Saraswati is worshipped on Vasant Panchami, a Hindu festival celebrated every year on the 5th lunar day in the Hindu calendar month of Magha (around January–February). On this day, Saraswati Puja is celebrated, people pray to Devi Saraswati for the gift of wisdom and enlightenment. Saraswati is the daughter of Shiva and Durga, and she also is the wife of Brahma.

Saraswati patronizes wisdom and arts and is identified as the inventor of Sanskrit. It is believed that she grants the talent of speech; the ability to communicate, carry and receive knowledge, to comprehend secret meanings of dharmas and to recognize the truth and separate it from the lie.

Education is light! That’s why Saraswati is portrayed as a white woman in a white dress sitting on a white lotus flower. She is adorned with white pearl beads and flowers. Saraswati has four arms, representing the four aspects of the human personality in cognition: mind, intellect, self-consciousness and ego. With two of her arms, she plays the music of love and life on a string instrument called a veena. This is a multi-stringed Indian musical instrument which possibilities range from a very sharp, buzzing sound, extremely rich in overtones to a clear and round sound with hardly any overtones, remotely resembling the sound of a guitar. It represents the fact that she is the patroness of fine arts. In her other two hands, Saraswati holds the Japamala which symbolizes inner reflection and a book representing all types of sacred knowledge.

The goddess is accompanied by a white swan and a peacock. White swan or Hamsa is a symbol of innocence, wisdom and discernment. Hamsa is a sacred bird, which if offered a mixture of milk and water, is said to be able to drink the milk alone separating water from it. It thus symbolizes the ability to distinguish between good and evil, to see the essence and separate the eternal from the evanescent. The peacock is a symbol of immortality and it also represents the immortality of true knowledge which has a divine origin. All the beauty of the infinite universe is imaged on the beautiful peacock’s tail.

As the scriptures say, this day should be spent in joy and dance, singing songs and playing musical instruments, honoring ancestors. The color of the Sri Panchami day is yellow: people put on new yellow clothes, prepare yellow sweets and treat each other with sun-colored fruits. This holiday is also considered as an excellent day for marriage and the naming ceremony.

Saraswati Day is not a national holiday in India but all schools are closed and the students take part in decorating places of worship. A few weeks before the holiday, schools often organize various music, sports and other competitions. Prizes are being given on the day of Vasant Panchami.

Another tradition on this holiday is flying kites which makes the holiday popular among children.

Sacred knowledge won’t come into a dark house or into a dark mind. Purity and light is the root of everything. Clean your room from rubbish and clutter, put on clean yellow clothes and spend some time reading mantras. You’ll free your consciousness from unnecessary information and the right work with mantras will bring you success, knowledge, vital energy and wisdom.

Mantra which gives wisdom, creative skills and talent in music:
OM AIM SARASWATYAI NAMAH.

Mantra related to creativity; it stimulates the work of the right hemisphere of the brain:
MANGALAM DISHTU ME SARASWATI.

Mantra for the improvement of cognitive skills and it also helps to cope with mental disorders and nervous breakdowns:
OM AIM NAMAH.

Mantra which gives vitality and energy:
OM AIM SHREEM HREEM SARASWATHI DEVYAI NAMAHA.

holiday.title: Ekadashi Fast
holiday.description:
This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: Imbolc
holiday.description:
On the night from February 1st to February 2nd, many countries celebrate the Imbolc holiday or St. Brigid's Day — the Celtic festival of purification, the glorification of the Sun, light and revival of the Earth.

This time is a midpoint between the winter solstice and the spring equinox and is associated with the approach of warmer weather and seasons changing. 

The holiday’s name Imbolc has old Irish roots as Mblec means "milk" because during this period sheep typically give birth to lambs and start lactating.

The holiday’s symbols are: Solar Wheel, Brigid's Cross, lights, lanterns, lamps and candles.

Imbolc is a time of purification, awakening and liberation from any clutter in your life, metaphorical too. Clean up the house, throw away old things and most importantly don’t forget to devote time to yourself. Try to let go of all negative thoughts and beliefs, open up to the approaching warmth and light.

On this day, it is not recommended to work, so take time to rest and relax, engage in meditation and take a bath with herbs, salts and aroma oils.

In addition, Imbolc is considered the ancestor of all family holidays, so this is a good reason to gather all family members at the holiday table.

For a joyful feast people usually prepared pancakes, meat with an abundance of spices, drank milk with honey and cinnamon, warm wine with dried berries and herbs.

holiday.title: Ekadashi Fast
holiday.description:
This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: Maha Shivaratri
holiday.description:
Maha Shivaratri is a Hindu festival in honor of the God Shiva. The holiday symbolizes the liberation of the mind from worldly thoughts, worship of the good and immersion in spirituality. Shivaratri is celebrated several times a year, as it falls on the night before the New Moon.

There are four types of Shivaratri: Nitya Shivaratri — every night, Masa Shivaratri — every New Moon, Magha Pratham-Adi Shivratri — 13 days before Maha Shivaratri and Maha Shivaratri itself. However, Maha Shivaratri is considered to be the most important one, and this is due to the special position of the Sun and the Moon.

According to legend, on this night Shiva performed the Tandava dance of primary creation, preservation and destruction. He promises his help to those who devote this time to spiritual practices. The worshipper will feel support in overcoming obstacles and inner experiences on the way to the onset of bliss and peace.

The purity of the body, mind and thoughts is the most important thing. The day should start with taking a bath or ablution in sacred reservoirs. Refrain from eating and drinking during the day.

Read sacred books or scriptures that energize and inspire you, meditate and pray for yourself and others, wishing for health, well-being and prosperity. Only pure thoughts and wishes are allowed because any meditation on this night is enhanced because of the power of the Sun and the Moon.

Repeat "Om Namah Shivaya" — "The worship of the Good!" completely immersed in awareness, in spiritual experience. Decorate your home with candles and lights.

Unmarried women can ask Parvati for a successful marriage and beautiful healthy children. Dedicate yourself to God, meditation and purification at least once a year.

Om Namah Shivaya!

holiday.title: Chinese New Year
holiday.description:
This holiday, better known as Chinese New Year, is celebrated on the second New Moon after the winter solstice from January 21st to February 21st. This holiday is spread throughout the world from Asia, where it is celebrated most vividly and protractedly for 15 days. Locals traditionally call it the Spring Festival.

Each Chinese New Year has a combination of different symbols: one of 12 zodiac animals, one color and one of the five elements (fire, wood, water, earth, metal).

According to legend, the celebration was originally a rite for salvation from the evil spirit of Nyan. It was afraid of the red colour and loud noises, that’s why red is considered to be the traditional color of the holiday. Fireworks go on throughout all nights of the celebration.

About a week before the New Year, people wherever they live, come to their hometown or village to celebrate the holiday with their families. They carry out general cleaning of the house, get rid of unnecessary things, purchase all that is needed. Houses and streets, entrance doors are decorated with red lamps, inscriptions, garlands.

On New Year's Eve, the whole family gathers for a big dinner. Traditional treats are dumplings, fish dishes and sweets. People discuss plans for the coming year and watch holiday programs on TV. The most common gift is a red envelope with money — Hongbao. In the following days of the celebration, street processions, masquerades and festivals are held.

holiday.title: Lakshmi Jayanti
holiday.description:
Lakshmi Jayanti is celebrated as the birth anniversary of Lakshmi Devi. This day is traditionally celebrated during the Full Moon in the month of Phalguna, known as Phalguna Purnima, Vasant Purnima or Madana Purnima. In some regions, Lakshmi Jayanti celebrations may begin a day earlier.

Lakshmi is one of the most powerful goddesses and she is very important in Hinduism. Lakshmi is a wife of Vishnu and she represents his energy. Vishnu demonstrates all the masculine strength and his beautiful wife is the embodiment of sensuality, spiritual purity and the symbolization of motherhood. Even the meaning of her name carries a bright and pure meaning: "good sign", "happiness" and “beauty”.

According to legend, Lakshmi appeared in a lotus flower from the waters of the milky ocean, during the confrontation between the Asuras (demons) and the Devas (gods) for the possession of the sacred elixir of Amrita.

Once upon a time, the king of the gods Indra was riding his faithful white elephant Ayravat when he met the Swami (yogi) Durvas Maharshi. As a sign of respect, the Swami gave the king a garland of flowers. The king accepted the gift and adorned the head of his elephant with it but the elephant did not like that and he threw it to the ground and trampled the garland.

Offended with this act, the Swami Durvasa Maharishi cursed the King Indra and all the other gods with the words: "All of you will lose your powers!" And so it happened. The gods tried to fix the situation but nothing helped so they asked Vishnu for help.

Vishnu promised them that the powers will be returned once a goddess appears from the ocean of milk. Soon after it came true.

During the churning of the ocean by devas and asuras, the goddess Lakshmi appeared in the lotus flower from the ocean of milk along with the sacred elixir Amrita. The powers returned to the gods and Vishnu took Lakshmi as his wife.

The beautiful goddess Lakshmi is described as the creature of extraordinary beauty; she is full of pure energy and her touch makes everything auspicious and divine.

Lakshmi Jayanti is a significant day in the Hindu culture. Practicing abstinence, performing rituals and reading mantras will be rewarded with favors from the goddess.

Start your day before dawn, take a bath and engage in the offering ritual. By tradition, the Goddess of prosperity loves when incense, flowers, fruits, valuable coins and new jewelry are offered to her. It is recommended to have only water and juices as meals that day, in rare cases, it is allowed to eat fresh fruits and vegetables.

Traditionally, people in India make donations to the Brahmins on that day; in the West, this custom may be replaced with helping those who are in need.

Reading mantras is an essential part of the celebration. The most common mantras are:

"Maha Lakshmi", which is a greeting to the goddess Lakshmi. "Great Lakshmi, destroy all troubles and bless abundance and prosperity on both the physical and spiritual planes in the future."

OM SHREEM MAHA LAKSHMIYEI NAMAHA

This mantra has a specific reading technique. It needs to be read line by line, in a specific way.

OM MAHALAKSHMYAI CHA VIDMAHE VISHNU PATNYAI CHA DHIMAHI TANNO LAKSHMIHI PRACHODAYAT

This mantra requires careful visualization when reading. If a woman reads it and visualizes a happy relationship with a man at the same time then the mantra will work to attract mutual love. If you imagine financial wellness, it will attract money and prosperity.

OM HREEM SHREEM LAKSHMI BHYO NAMAHA

It is very important to have pure intentions when reading mantras. Wishing love has to be mutual and the enrichment must be reached by fair means.

holiday.title: Holi
holiday.description:
This is a colorful Indian holiday, symbolizing the arrival of spring and the beginning of the New Year. It takes place in early spring, at the end of February or in the beginning of March and is celebrated for three days: it begins on the Full Moon day (last day) in the month of Phalguna (February–March), and continues to the next day — the first day of the Chaitra month (March–April).

It is believed that previously it was one of the special rituals during which married women worshiped the Full Moon to attract happiness and prosperity into their families.

There are many legends about the origin of this holiday but the most common is about the young man Prahlada, the son of the omnipotent Hiranyakasipa, who had mystical power and was almost invulnerable. Hiranyakashipu enslaved the entire universe but his son refused to obey the father’s will and began to worship Vishnu. This behavior irritated his father and he gave an order to kill his son but there was no weapon that could destroy him, and after that Hiranyakashipu asked his sister, the demoness Holika, who was fire resistible, to come into the fire with the rebellious young man. Holika took Prahlada in her arms and entered the fire. But something incredible happened: by the will of Vishnu, Prahlada came out of the fire unharmed but the demoness Holika burned to ashes.

Enraged Vishnu came up to Hiranyakashipu in the guise of Nrsimhadeva — half-lion, half-man. He grabbed Hiranyakashipu and tore him to pieces. This is how the world was saved from a terrible demon.

An important element of the first day of the Holi celebration is the symbolic burning of the evil demoness Holika, personifying the evil and coldness of winter.

Preparation for the festival begins a month before: there are small celebrations held, ritual games with songs and dances, glorifying the victory of Vishnu. Branches, rags and straws are collected to make a scarecrow representing Holika. On the first day of the celebration of Holi the scarecrow of the demon Holika which represents cold and evil is burned. Sometimes a specially decorated tree is burned instead of a scarecrow.

On the second day, members of all castes and age groups sprinkle each other with a colored powder called Gulal, made from colored cornmeal. The whole city, every inhabitant and every animal passing by are covered with colored paints on this day. The main color of the holiday is red. It is believed that the more paint is coated on a person’s clothes, the more good wishes are directed towards them.

Holi symbolizes the arrival of spring and the beginning of a new year, and it is important to meet a new year of life with pure thoughts and clear mind. Take a bath and put on bright clothes. If it’s possible, attend a nearby festival. It is important not only to participate in the battle of colors but to put the meaning into action. With every handful of colored powder thrown, you get rid of the problems of the past year and attract luck.

holiday.title: International Women's Day

It is important to remember that International Women's Day makes no difference between feminists and conservatives, housewives and businesswomen, adults and girls — this is a holiday for every woman because each of them has her own charm. Think how amazing it is to be a woman, remember what you learned and what wisdom you gained. Congratulate all dear to heart women and show how much you love them in one way or another.

This day is perfect to indulge in a little pampering session: take a bath with essential oils, buy or cook something nice and tasty for yourself, wear comfortable clothes. You can buy flowers or plants in the pot, light up scented candles and incense. It is also good to dive into doing something you, as creation is auspicious for all women. holiday.title: World Sleep Day
holiday.description:
Every year just before the Vernal Equinox, World Sleep Day is held. It was established by the World Sleep Day Committee of the World Sleep Society, to promote a healthy lifestyle and the need of proper, healthy sleep.

Harmony of body and soul is possible only if we can synchronize our biorhythms with the natural cycles and processes of the Universe. When we break the regime, we are weakened physically and mentally and tend to become vulnerable to diseases, lose connection with people around us and ourselves.

According to the Vedic Law of Time, a person should go to bed no later than 10 pm and get up with the Sun (from 4 am to 6 am). Total sleep time should be at least 6–7 hours. From 9 pm you should not engage in activity and work. While asleep, our body charges with physical and mental energy under the influence of the forces of the Moon, and also produces the hormone melatonin which is necessary for beauty and youth. After waking up, you should take a cool, refreshing shower, put on clean clothes, do light exercises and have breakfast before 7 am. Also, the most favorable time for meditation and spiritual practices comes after awakening, when the sun has not yet risen.

Such a regime, in accordance with the Solar and Lunar cycles, harmonizes our vital energy, makes us alert, happy and full of strength.

holiday.title: Ekadashi Fast
holiday.description:
This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: Vedic New Year
holiday.description:
Chaitra Navaratri is a Vedic festival that marks the beginning of the new astrological year. It starts on the first day of the Waxing Moon in the month of Chaitra (March-April) and coincides with the New Moon in Pisces.

Navaratri is celebrated twice a year (in spring and autumn). It is a nine-day festival dedicated to the nine forms of the great goddess Durga, symbolizing purification, the victory of light over darkness, and truth over ignorance.

Pisces is the last sign of the zodiac, marking the completion of one cycle and the preparation for a new beginning. That is why the New Moon in this sign is a powerful time for letting go of the past and setting new intentions.

How to Celebrate the Festival

— Dedicate time to purification

The energy of the next nine days is ideal for releasing old patterns and negative emotions. It is beneficial to take a salt bath, maintain the purity of body and mind, and follow a light, clean diet (fruits, nuts, grains) while avoiding heavy foods and alcohol. You can also clean your home, perform an energetic cleansing using incense or bell sounds, and engage in forgiveness and release practices. The meditations in the Healing section — “Mountain River,” “Clearing Unconscious Patterns,” and “Letting Go of Resentment” — can support you in this process.

— Reflect and express gratitude

Take time to thank the past year for its lessons and experiences. Keeping a gratitude journal for nine days can be a powerful practice. You may also listen to the meditation “Gratitude to Yourself”.

— Set intentions for the upcoming year

Write down five key goals for the new year, engage in manifestation and visualization rituals, or create a vision board. The meditation “Perfect Future” can help you focus your intentions.

— Connect with divine energies

Listening to the Durga mantra can awaken your inner strength. Ask the goddess for protection, assistance in overcoming obstacles, and support in new beginnings.

Chaitra Navaratri marks the beginning of a new path, the victory over inner fears and limitations. It is not just a festival but a time for spiritual renewal and deep self-work. May this Lunar New Year bring you harmony, prosperity, and inner strength! 🌙✨

From here comes the concept of positive and negative karma of a person which can be seen in the astrology birth chart.

Thus, working with the astrologist, you can find out your potential and see the strengths and weaknesses of your soul, as well as gain knowledge on how to improve life through spiritual awakening and purification of karma.

Patron saint of astrology is Ganesha, the god of knowledge and wisdom with the face of an elephant. He has power over earthly feelings and affections, allows people to comprehend the truth and grants good luck. Mantras of Ganesha, for example, OM GAM GANAPATAYE NAMAHA, removes all obstacles in a person’s path, giving them purity of intent, prosperity, and galore.

holiday.title: Rama Navami
holiday.description:
Rama Navami or the birthday of Rama is a week during which we celebrate the appearance of the seventh embodiment of powerful Vishnu — Lord Rama. Vishnu is the keeper of the Universe and one of the most revered gods of Hinduism. He maintains and rules life in the Universe. In the seventh incarnation, he expresses himself as an ideal ruler who came to confirm the path of dharma.

Rama Navami is the day of the appearance of Rama as an avatar of God Vishnu, who came to defeat the demon Ravana. Rama's victory symbolizes the victory of good over evil. The holiday lasts for a week. It is also called the week of the ancient Indian epic Ramayana. This is one of the most significant sacred texts of Hinduism — Smriti. Ramayana combines 24,000 verses!

On this day, it is customary to read passages from the Ramayana, take part in Shobha Yatra — a colorful procession and swim in the Sarayu River. Fast is observed: some people adhere to it only on the first day before sunset, others do it throughout the whole week. At the end of the festival, Prasada is distributed. Rama baby figurines are washed with water, dressed and put into a cradle.

Refrain from eating onions and wheat products; when fasting try to consume only fruits and vegetables. As the name implies, Rama Navami is a great time to listen and read the Ramayana, as well as sing bhajans and kirtans glorifying Rama, his wife Sita and Hanuman.

holiday.title: Earth Hour
holiday.description:
Earth Hour is an unusual event when people turn off the lights and electrical appliances in houses for one hour — lights are also extinguished on all popular monuments and sights. WWF organized this campaign in 2007 and since then 188 countries, more than 2 billion people join in every year. The main aim of Earth Hour is not to reduce electrical usage but to draw people's attention to environmental problems.

If you want to join a common initiative and become a part of a social movement, you can turn off the light for one hour. Spend the evening with your family engaging in a conversation instead of a silly TV show and playing with your smartphone. Make everyone a nice cup of tea and go down a memory lane with your close ones.

A lot of events dedicated to environmental problems are held on Earth Day. Look out for such activities in your city: it can be community workday, bike ride, a lecture or volunteer day. For real energy-saving you can make simple changes in your daily life: for example, wash clothes with cooler water, fill up the washing machine at least 70–80%, repair leaking taps, use energy-saving light bulbs, reduce the use of heaters and air conditioners and of course don’t forget to turn off the lights when you leave. Let more air and sunlight into the house, use the natural resources as effectively as you can and Nature will thank you.

holiday.title: International Birds Day
holiday.description:
The holiday is celebrated on April 1st. At this time migratory birds return to their native lands, filling the world with singing. The holiday is dedicated to the conservation of all species of birds, especially those that are threatened with extinction. Birds are not only incredible creatures but also an important part of a natural system. Without them harmony in the world is impossible.

Birds have always been considered mythical creatures, the personification of freedom and the human soul. According to Slavic traditions, feeding birds bring good luck and financial well-being. The idea of reincarnation in many religions is that all of us in different lives can become animals or birds. Compassion and helping all living beings improve karma and fill the heart with love.

This day may become an occasion to learn something new about birds and how to help them. It is especially important to explain this to children. For example, how to distinguish a fallen chick from a fledgling — a young bird that learns to fly under the control of its parents and which must not be taken home. Or that you should never disturb nests no matter the reason — birds will not return to the chicks, and they are doomed to death. These are living beings, therefore they cannot be used in rituals. Tradition to release birds for the Annunciation or for the harmonization of Saturn gives poachers the basis for the bird trade. Birds are kept in terrible conditions and then cannot survive in nature. The best ritual with birds is to feed them in the wild, listen to them chirp and find peace of mind.

Remember that we are all part of the same Universe. When caring for others, you become closer to the Earth and your natural beginning.

holiday.title: Hanuman Jayanti
holiday.description:
This holiday is dedicated to the Hindu deity Hanuman, who symbolizes courage, selfless humility and devotion. Hanuman, who is also called Anjaneya — the leader of the Vanaras who are half-humans, half-monkeys and are great warriors. Hanuman himself is also often depicted in a monkey-like appearance. He is the son of the god of air and wind Vayu and the apsara of Punjistala.

The cult of Hanuman is one of the most popular in Hinduism today because Hanuman is known for his friendliness. He is considered the patron of science and research, as well as rural life.

Most of the states of India celebrate Hanuman Jayanti on the Full Moon of the month of Chaitra (March - April). Hanuman was born at dawn on the Full Moon.

The holiday begins at dawn in houses and temples with sacred chants (kirtans) and puja — rites of worship. Praising hymns — chalisas are heard everywhere. Hanuman is presented with sindur, fruits (especially bananas) and betel.

It is believed that the veneration of Hanuman during the year creates a good attitude of deity towards you and allows you to share some of his characteristics: courage, determination, devotion to belief. Hanuman’s strength symbolizes the unlimited potential and strength that are inherent in everyone.

On Hanuman Jayanti, it is good to light candles and aroma lamps near the images of the deity in order to attract his grace. Hanuman is usually associated with red colour, so on his birthday put on clothes and jewelry that are orange and red. In food, it is best to choose red fruits and vegetables.

It is favourable to read Hanuman Chalisa and Hanuman Ashtaku, as well as mantras.

The Moola Mantra of Hanuman is one of the main mantras of Hanuman. It protects from dangerous situations, helps in overcoming difficulties and in achieving well-being. Repeat OM SHRI HANUMATE NAMAHA.

The Gayatri Mantra of Hanuman is a mantra that protects from dangers and negative influence of planets, in particular Saturn and Mars. OM ANJANAYA VIDMAHE VAYYUPUTRAYA DHIMAHI TANNO HANNUMAT PRACHODAYAT.

And if you are lucky enough to get a chance to feed a monkey with a banana today — be sure to seize the opportunity, it will certainly bring good luck!

holiday.title: Ekadashi Fast
holiday.description:
This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: The beginning of a new Solar Year

Indians prepare very carefully for the holiday. It all starts with decorating the house with flowers and hanging embroidered images of the gods. Then they traditionally gather near the sacred river Ganges and perform ritual ablutions. The banks of the river become sites for festive performances and colorful fireworks displays. Religious music can be heard everywhere and festively dressed people wish each other a happy new year.

Cleansing from sins is the main goal of festive ablution in the sacred river. And of course it’s not possible, one can take a bath instead. Start the day by decorating your home and preparing a rich festive table because the New Year in any country is a holiday of galore and contentment.

The beginning of a new Solar year is well-suited for making plans for the next year.

holiday.title: Akshaya Tritiya
holiday.description:
Akshaya Tritiya is one of the strongest and most auspicious days in the Vedic calendar. Akshaya from ancient Sanskrit translates as "invincible, indestructible" and Tritiya means the third lunar day which is considered the most favourable day for new beginnings.

The festival takes place once a year when the Sun and the Moon are in signs of their strongest manifestation which is called exaltation (the Sun in Aries and the Moon in Taurus) and falls on the third lunar day.

Akshaya Tritiya is the day of multiplication of goodness. It’s considered the most favourable period for various achievements, spiritual practices, starting something new and helping others. All good beginnings are multiplied, both in the spiritual and material spheres because the strongest energies of the Sun contribute to this. 

To bring good into your life, you need to prepare yourself properly and clear your life of everything that can burden you. You can clean the house the day before and get rid of old unnecessary things. It is desirable to carry out energy cleaning of the house to purify the aura and for this purpose, you can use salt, fire (candles, incense or Palo Santo) or water (charged by the sun or moon). Pay special attention to all corners around the house and hard-to-reach places. During energy cleansing, you can say a prayer, mantra or just keep a positive internal mood that will help your home to be cleansed of physical and mental debris.

Besides, it is worth taking care of the purity of the mind and body. Forgive the wrongdoers, pay your debts, perform ablutions, say a mantra or prayer, perform a meditation concentrating on purification and healing — all this will ease your spirit and help it to reach a new level of development. Observing the fast will help to strengthen the favourable energies of this day.

It is good if you can start your day outdoors or in sacred places, temples, attend a service or Puja. Service can manifest itself in caring for animals and helping those in need.
Akshaya Tritiya is also called the day of fulfilment of dreams. The energy of the day is so strong that it will definitely help your wishes come true but only if they bring good to others. On this day you must make your wish list.

Traditionally in India, on this day people buy gold and silver believing that precious metals will bring wealth. The day is very favourable for weddings, engagements, moving and starting school. Children conceived on that day shall be happy and lucky throughout their life.

Everything created with good intentions on this day is destined for success and multiplication. Don't miss the opportunity to make positive changes in your life. It is also important to know that this day is suitable for various undertakings only if in global astrology there are no negative positions of the planets that would interfere with favourable energies of the Sun and the Moon.

Thousands of liters of water per kilogram are spent on meat production and forests are cut down for the sake of pastures. If it is difficult for you to switch to a vegetarian diet completely, try to reduce meat consumption as much as possible according to your needs — even this simple step will save natural resources. Remember that every little counts. Also if you have a lot of unnecessary books or clothes, you can donate them to charities. This way you give new life to things and bring happiness to other people.

Every year May 3rd is dedicated to the celebration of World Sun Day. The purpose of the holiday is to remind us that the use of renewable natural resources is environmentally friendly and is a proper way to generate energy. There are various presentations of solar panels, electric vehicles and other environmentally friendly products.

The Sun is the center of the Universe, a life-giving source of light and cosmic energy for all living things. In Vedic astrology, it corresponds to the Graha Surya which in the natal chart determines the true Self of humans, their personality and character. The Sun is a male planet and bestows such qualities as inner strength, individuality and leadership. Male energy helps to take care of others, take responsibility and create a world around us.

The Sun symbolizes a father, a man. In the natal chart of a woman, it can determine her relationship with the opposite gender. In a body, the Sun is responsible for health and the skeleton. Surya shows a predisposition to professions and paves the way for self-knowledge.

In order to live in harmony with the Sun, you should often take walks out in the fresh air, eat more fruits and vegetables and try to wake up before sunrise. Start your day with a set of yoga exercises Surya Namaskar — it will fill you with energy and strength. You can also read and listen to the mantras of the Sun, for example, OM HRAM HRIM HRAUM SAHA SURYAYA NAMAHA.

They say that in order to see God, one must raise their head and look at the Sun. It contains the power of happiness that will fill your life with new colors. Living in harmony with the luminary, you also become a source of light.

holiday.title: Mother’s Day
holiday.description:
Today is an international holiday dedicated to mothers. Traditionally in many countries, it is held on the second Sunday of May.

The symbol of Mother’s Day is forget-me-not flower. It is believed that it has a magic power to bring back memories of people who were forgotten by their relatives and beloved ones.

Mother is associated with love, harmony and care. But first of all, every mother is a woman. Female energy, sensitivity, intuition, beauty and happiness are under control of the Moon. It is the main planet for women, considered as Mother of all planets that personifies selfless mother’s love and care.

It is favorable to meditate on the Moon, to sing mantras, for example, OM CHANDRAYA NAMAHA, OM NAMO BHAGAVATE VASUDEVAYA, as they give harmony and peace of mind. By devoting the whole day to your mother you pay tribute to the Moon and make its influence much stronger.

The bond with the mother is one of the strongest in our lives. Mother gives life, protects the child, first within her body and then in the outside world. 

Throughout her life, she shares endless love and care with the child. Mother and the Kin will forever remain an important part of us. Everyone carries the image of the inner mother, which determines their ability to be mindful of themselves and others, to love and build strong relationships.

On this day, you can congratulate your mother, say words of love and gratitude to her, give flowers and arrange an activity for both of you. Try to spend this day in harmony with yourself and with your mother.

If you do not have the opportunity to be with your mother, you can take time to think about her, pray for her, write her a sincere letter and light candles. You can turn to the inner image of the mother and establish contact with her within yourself. Upayas to the Moon can help with this, for example, the mantra Om Chandraya Namah, as well as fasting on Mondays and meditation. Also, to harmonize the internal image of the mother, you can turn to a psychologist and a master of any tradition, work to eliminate resentful and negative patterns and use the family constellations approach.

holiday.title: Ekadashi Fast
holiday.description:
This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: International climate day
holiday.description:
Climate Day is celebrated around the world on May 15th. The holiday helps to draw people's attention to the problems that arise on our planet. In addition to the fact that climate change occurs naturally, the huge impact is made by people themselves of course.

For the first time, the problem of climate change was internationally discussed 30 years ago and in 1992 during the Convention on climate change that was held in Rio de Janeiro as part of the Earth Summit. But "the globalization machine" worked at full power at this time already — there are more and more products every year, forests are being cut down, some of them burned in fires and more cattle to feed all people are grown at scary high rates. The consequences of such actions can be irreversible if we do not focus on them.

Now environmentalists all over the world hold thematic events on this day, start projects on waste-free consumption and day by day tirelessly talk about the problem and offer all sorts of alternative solutions. Undoubtedly, environmental problems are the business of each of us and the increasing level of awareness of this is pleasing.

Everyone can start with themselves.

First of all, you should revise your daily life: what things surround you, what materials they are made of, what you have not used for a long time, what is not useful anymore, what you can refuse or replace and how to recycle it environmentally friendly. Surrounding physical objects and space also bring their own energy to the owner and after clearing them, you can see how the filling of new energy occurs.

The next important step will be to help our Home — the Earth. You can organize a cleaning session near your home or on the entire street on your own and involve your neighbors. A great solution is to clear the forest or the shore of the pond/lake/sea and you may also ask your relatives, friends or neighbors to help. This is a powerful practice that cleanses the space not only outside but also inside. It unites people with nature, energizes and leads to positive changes.

Such simple and regular practices can radically change the life of both the person and the environment, creating a channel for a new flow of energy, ideas and opportunities. The main thing to remember is that everything starts with baby steps.

holiday.title: Shani Jayanti
holiday.description:
Shani Jayanti is a special day in the Indian tradition, the birthday of Saturn, its embodiment in the material world. The celebration begins with the onset of Amavasya Tithi (New Moon), during the month of Jyestha (May–June).

Saturn, the brother of the death god Yamaraja, is the supreme heaven judge who pays us for our sins, impartially and fairly punishes or bestows. However, only such strict observer can instill in people qualities necessary for spiritual growth: control of feelings and actions, discipline, devotion, patience, humility.

On this day, religious ceremonies and charity events are held in India. Saturn likes when we help people and animals in need. Traditional donation is black rice and black sesame.

Celebrators visit the temples of Shani Deva or visit forests to meditate and recite mantras. Some people go on a spiritual strike — spiritual practice of voluntary refusal or restriction.

Shani is responsible for karmic retribution, illness, obstacles and suffering that can affect everyone. That's why it’s important we don’t lose a chance to worship him.

Help people and animals in need, feed them or cure them. Visit your elderly relatives. Respect and love will improve both their and your conditions.

If you feel you need a spiritual strike, then go for it. It can be a day without food, meditation on the floor, a vow of silence for a day or reading of the scriptures throughout the night.

Honor Shani by reading the mantra: Om Shanicharaya Namah — Om I express my respect to Shani.

Auspicious time for reading the mantra is early morning or evening.  It's recommended to read this mantra at least 108 times

holiday.title: The Purushottama month
holiday.description:
The sacred month of Purushottama is an additional, thirteenth lunar month, which occurs only once every 2 years and 8 months.

It’s believed that the Purushottama month has the strongest impact on a person's karma because it’s the Supreme Lord Krishna himself who protects and favours this month. All the consequences of our thoughts and actions are multiplied. Therefore, negative actions may later result in very unpleasant scenarios while good actions such as purification, forgiveness practices and asceticism become incredibly powerful and effective. During this period, it’s best not to concentrate your attention on material aspects of life but to direct it towards spiritual growth and karma cleansing.

Try to wake up with the sunrise during this month, spend some time reading mantras and prayers, study the holy scriptures and get involved with the charity. It’s important to have good intentions and not to expect anything in return when doing good deeds. Any ancestral practices and austerities aimed at family karma purification, acquire special power this month. When it comes to food intake, remember that moderation is the key: refrain from meat and stodgy products and stick to moderate-sized portions. If you find it difficult to fast for a whole month, you can keep fast on two unique Ekadashi — Padmini Ekadashi and Parama Ekadashi, as well as the very powerful five-day fast of Pancharatrika, which begins immediately after Parama Ekadashi.

In the month of Purushottama, it’s better to avoid large purchases, major undertakings, haircuts and sexual relations. Refrain from lies, insults and do not cause harm to anyone whether with words, deeds or thoughts. Living this month with an open heart and a pure soul will cleanse your karma and attract prosperity and happiness into your life.

holiday.title: Children's Day
holiday.description:
Children's day is celebrated all over the world on June 1st. This holiday was established after the Second World War due to the fact that many children were left without parents, homes and livelihoods and were in desperate need of support of any kind.

Since then, a lot of time has passed and now International Children's Day is a holiday dedicated not only to children’s in need but also to spreading information regarding various aspects of education and improving the quality of life of young members of society.

We should try to help our children and contribute to their happiness on any day of the year but on Children's Day you can explore and participate in events around your town and pay a visit to certain entertainment programs, educational and developmental activities.

Since school-age children are about to start their summer holidays very soon, you can start discussing the pros and cons of the past school year with your child, make plans for the next year and plan fun summer adventures together.

The most important qualities that need to be instilled in every child are kindness and empathy, so on this day, you can talk to children about mutual understanding, help and the ability to listen to other people.
The most important thing is to show your child that you love them and accept them for who they are. If you don't have your own child, you can give gifts to the children of your relatives or friends, do something good for orphans or children from disadvantaged families.

Each one of us has an inner child who is responsible for how we perceive the world, for our emotions, openness, creativity and most importantly the ability to enjoy life. This is your first and most sincere expression of personality that influences everything that happens now. If your inner child is buried deep down inside of you, having no outlet then this is expressed by a sense of insecurity, weakness, low self-esteem and distrust in people around you. On the other hand, if your inner child is too spoiled and rambunctious then this will manifest itself as infantilism, irresponsibility and dependence on others.

Many internal blocks and fears take their roots in our childhood. The ability to connect and heal your inner child helps to work with those blocks and fears, get rid of certain barriers and learn to love yourself. There is a powerful meditation that can provide healing for your inner child and help invoke him/her, engage in dialogue and ask about his/hers feelings and thoughts. You can do this by keeping a diary or writing a series of letters. You can also engage in activities and hobbies that you loved during your childhood, work on fulfilling your childhood dreams. If you have problems finding common grounds when it comes to communication with kids then it is beneficial to turn to the powerful mantra of Krishna — the Santan Gopal mantra, which harmonizes karma when it comes to children.

holiday.title: Ekadashi Fast
holiday.description:
This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: Global Wind Day
holiday.description:
June 15th marks World Wind Day (Global Wind Day). This holiday is quite young and was born in Europe in 2007 and two years later it began to be celebrated on four continents of our planet. Internationally, the goal of the festival is to draw attention to the potential of wind power.

For the first time, the wind was used as a source of energy by Sinhalese people that lived near the city of Anuradhapura and in some other areas of Sri Lanka. They have used monsoon winds to light their stoves already by the end of IV century BC.

From a scientific point of view, wind power has a huge potential and it is actively used in the form of wind power plants in many countries including the United States, China, Spain and Germany. On this day, seminars and lectures on wind energy are held in many countries as well as excursions to wind substations.

For our ancestors the wind was the personification of one or more gods, it was endowed with supernatural powers, it was worshipped and even sacrificed.

Thus, the Hindu God of wind Vayu plays an important role in the mythology of the Upanishads where he is the father of Bhima and the spiritual father of Hanuman. In the Japanese Shinto tradition one of the oldest gods is the wind God Fujin. According to the legend, he already existed at the time of the creation of the world and released the winds from his bag to clear the world from the mist. In ancient Greek mythology, there were four gods at once — Boreas (North Wind), Notus (South Wind), Eurus (East Wind) and Zephyrus (West Wind) and demigod Aeolus ruled over them.

According to Ayurveda, the primary elements that underlie the material world are composed of several combinations or Doshas — they are Vata, Pitta and Kapha. In a balanced state, Doshas support the human body as three pillars but in normal life, one or two Doshas are more often predominant. Vata means "fast” and "windy” Dosha and represents the bodily air. "Wind" makes you hesitant when it comes to making decisions, causes mood swings and is responsible for movement. To harmonize the Vata Dosha slow and calm practices with a combination of Ujjayi Pranayama, Nadi Shodhana Pranayama, as well as Agnisara Dhauti and Kapalabhati can help.

In astrology, the signs of the air element include Gemini, Libra and Aquarius. They symbolize the flexibility of the mind, intelligence, the desire to learn new things and philosophy. People of the air element can find the shortest way to solve problems and surprise others with their ability to do several things at once.

The element of wind is very versatile and interesting to study from different points of view and on this day you can feel unity with it through the practice of yoga Nidra, Pranayama practice and Om chant meditation. You can also sign up for a lecture or an excursion to a wind substation or even fly a kite in the sky with your children.

holiday.title: Father’s Day
holiday.description:
Father's Day is celebrated on the third Sunday of June in many countries. The idea of the holiday was proposed by one woman as a sign of gratitude and love for her father. Her mother died early and her father raised six children alone, becoming everything to them.

In different countries, traditions of celebration might vary. People congratulate their fathers, gather at the family table and/or go out. They pay respects to those men who have passed away. There are support groups and meetings to help families with many children and single fathers providing psychological training to help them raise children.

Vedic culture gives an important role to fathers in a child's life. The personification of a man, a father in the natal chart and destiny is the Sun. Its position defines the main traits of character, human's place in the world. Bad relationships with father disrupt contact with the Sun.

Father contributes an inevitable part providing life energy into the child. His influence affects sons' image of male behavior in general and of course moral boundaries. For girls, it affects future relationships with men and her self-confidence.

Honoring parents is one of the main virtues of each person. Our birth is a great miracle and parents are the creators who made this miracle happen. Obligatory day for honouring father is Sunday, day of the Sun.

According to the Vedas, a person can have five fathers: leader of the country, spiritual mentor, biological father, stepfather and the one who supports the person. Father's Day is another reason to tell your father how much you love and treasure him.

holiday.title: International kissing day
holiday.description:
World kissing day or international kissing day is celebrated around the world on July 6th. It is an unofficial national holiday but is vividly celebrated in more than 60 countries around the world.

The birthplace of this tender holiday is Great Britain. There exactly the decision was made that the kiss was worthy of having its own celebration. On this day festivals, parades and favorite contests "for the longest kiss", "the most unusual kiss", etc. are held. The traditional color of the holiday is red — the color of passion, love and fervor as well as pink — the color of tenderness and fragility. But unfortunately, not in all corners of our planet people honor and love kisses. In some countries, they are considered the height of indecency and some people do not know about them at all!

The world is still arguing about the origin of the kiss and its sacred meaning. A kiss is a sacrament of the reunion of two organisms and the exchange of energy, a way to show your affection. So there is a belief that the moment when a mother fed her child through her mouth with chewed food ("feeding kiss") was the origin of the kiss as an action. According to another theory, the kiss is inherent. Kisses used to come and go, being unpopular during some times. They were banned in the Middle Ages because of the possibility of transmitting terrible diseases and returned after a long time, as the priests realized its sacred necessity.

The strongest esoteric quality of a kiss is the protection of the body. The contact of lips and tongues enables astral protection and activates the chakras. This pleasant ritual creates a kind of energy framework that prevents magical attacks and negative effects. In the same way, the kiss acts as a "vaccination". The exchange of microflora and fluids during a kiss gives an impetus to the body to develop a protective field against possible diseases, thereby increasing the immune system.

People all over the world vividly celebrate this important holiday by creating strong energy threads on the earth. Join in with your partner, take part in the fun or spend the day alone, because as Plato said, "A kiss is an exchange between two souls." If you do not have a partner then by all means go to a festive event and recharge with the energy of others.

holiday.title: World Whale and Dolphin Day
holiday.description:
On July 23rd, the whole world celebrates World Whale and Dolphin Day to commemorate the ban on whale fishing and the brutal extermination of marine inhabitants. Every year on this day there are events that are aimed at protecting underwater mammals, forums where you can listen to their voices and even touch imitation material of their skin. In maritime cities, training is provided on how to assist marine animals that have been caught ashore or got into nets.

Many countries have adopted the Declaration of Rights for Cetaceans: Whales and Dolphins. They should be perceived as individuals with minds and feelings, and of course, all animals should. Marine mammals cannot be kept in captivity and made anyone's property. In India, dolphins are recognized as creatures with a high level of consciousness.

In the underwater world, dolphins have created their own civilization just like humans. They have high intelligence and self-awareness. Dolphins live in families taking care of each other. They have their own culture and traditions that they pass on to their descendants. There are many known cases when dolphins came to help and rescue people.

People at all times admired these mysterious creatures. As a sign of respect, there is a small beautiful constellation of Dolphin and a major constellation of Whale in the northern part of the skyscraper. The stars line up in a curved line, like a whale that has bent its tail and opened its mouth. In the ancient civilization of Māori dolphins and whales were a symbol of protection, representing the unity of humans with the sea and the surrounding world. The dolphin-shaped charm was given to travelers as an amulet.

There are methods that include dolphin therapy for people who have undergone mental trauma or who suffer from diseases. It is especially effective for children: communication with dolphins becomes a social model for them which helps to interact with others. Thanks to the incredible energy of these animals, a sense of happiness and higher peace come to people. But one must remember — only interact with dolphins in their natural habitat, and never in any kinds of dolphinariums or aquariums. Do not support those facilities as they only harm those beautiful creatures.

Whales are the only undersea creatures who can sing. Their songs through underwater acoustic channels can reach another hemisphere of the planet. Songs differ in different kinds and are transmitted from generation to generation. Whales sing to their beloved, lull their babies to sleep with lullabies. What they sing about remains a mystery to this day. But this extraordinary underwater music creates a whole world unfathomable to us.

This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: Guru Purnima
holiday.description:
Guru Purnima or Day of the Guru or Vyasa Purnima is the day of veneration of Ved Vyasa, the first guru and sage who wrote the famous "Mahabharata". Vyasa added to the sacred Veda collection and also wrote 18 sacred Puranas of Hinduism. He was the guru (teacher) of Dattatreya, who is considered the Master of the Masters.

Guru Purnima is celebrated every year on the Full Moon of the month of Ashadha (June–July). The Full Moon is not an accidental choice for the holiday because the Moon conveys a reflection of the glow of the Sun, as a guru connects God and man, nullifying the darkness of human ignorance. In Hinduism, it is believed that on this day Vyasa began to write the Vedanta-sutras — a treatise containing the Vedas philosophy.

Spiritual mentors and their followers worship Vyasa on Guru Purnima, performing puja — a ceremony of veneration — and express their gratitude to him. Pupils give gifts to their teachers and fall at their feet to receive a blessing. The practice of worshiping teachers provides an opportunity to receive blessings on their spiritual path. In temples and ashrams (places of residence of sages and hermits), celebrations are held with reading the scriptures and treats.

This day is considered suitable to find a teacher that will help you along your way, if you don't already have one. Chaturmasya, the annual holy fast, also begins on this day. During this period, the guru and his or her students retire and study the sacred texts, engaging in philosophical conversations.

First of all, Guru Day is a favorable day for reading and congratulating teachers, giving them gifts and remembering mentors. You can also make a donation to spiritual people, listen and read various mantras and fast.

On Guru Purnima gratitude to the Guru can be expressed via a mantra:

GURUR BRAHMA
GURUR VISHNU
GURU DEVO MAHESHVARAHA
GURU SAAKSHAT PARA BRAHMA
TASMAI SRI GURAVE NAMAHA

This mantra is dedicated to the Teacher because only the Guru or Teacher can open the path to God.

In addition, Vyasa Purnima is a great day to begin spiritual practice — Sadhana. On this day, the veneration of Vyasa is expressed by giving him flowers and incense.

holiday.title: Pachamama Day
holiday.description:
Pachamama Day is a celebration of the ancient Inca tribes and their descendants who lived in the Andean region. To this day, it's still celebrated by the people of Bolivia, Chile, Ecuador, Argentina and Peru.

The day is dedicated to the goddess Pachamama (from the language of the Quechua Indians: "pacha" — world, universe, "mama" — mother). She is considered to be the goddess of earth and fertility. She governs weather, bestows abundant harvest and livestock, and contributes to creating a new life. She is held in high regard as a progenitor of all living things, and people ask her for protection, support and good luck.

The Indians believe that Pachamama is worn out and exhausted by the time winter solstice comes around, which is on June 21st in the southern hemisphere. She needs 40 days to rest and by August, she gains strength again like a woman after the birth of a child and begins a new life cycle. Therefore, the day of paying tribute to Mother Earth falls on August 1st.

At all times, the indigenous people worshiped Pachamama and were afraid of her anger. It was customary to bring her offerings such as sweets, wine and corn beer, as well as tobacco and sacrificial meat. Everything was put into a hole dug in the ground and burned in order to please the goddess. Also, people built "apachets" (apachita) — sacred pyramids made of stones, and "ilya" (illa) — from logs in her honor. They were put up near the cattle pens or, when traveling, on the mountain slopes, as a gratitude to the goddess for a safe journey.

Nowadays, the Indians, who honor the traditions of their ancestors, gather with their families and invite guests. They clean houses, burn incense and resin. People still put gifts for the goddess into the hole, except for meat, as in modern customs, animals are not sacrificed anymore. After the festive feast, it's time for fun and dancing, which usually lasts until early morning.

Pachamama Day is a celebration of life in all its glory. It is favorable to spend time outdoors, get closer to earth — have a picnic, do yoga outdoors, walk barefoot, engage in Earth meditation. Any grounding practices will be especially effective and bring harmony to your body and soul today. You can find out more about them in the article Earthing, which is in the Wisdom section. On this day, it will also be beneficial to engage in Earth Energy meditation that can be found in Healing's Vitality section.

holiday.title: Shravan Somwar Vrat
holiday.description:
Shravan, the fifth month in the Indian calendar is dedicated to the divine Shiva. On the first Monday of the month, the Shravan Somvar Vrat fast begins (from Sanskrit "somvar” — Monday, "vrat" — vow, fasting). It’s a powerful practice for family well-being and love. According to the legend, the goddess Parvati observed strict austerity on Mondays for 16 000 years and was blessed to become the wife of the great Shiva.

Fasting can be observed by unmarried women to gain a beloved man, who will be as handsome and perfect as Shiva. Married women with the help of the practice harmonize family relations, strengthen love and marriage. Men can also fast to gain peace and happiness. Shravan Somvar Vrat attracts the blessing of Shiva and improves family karma.

It is auspicious to fast for sixteen Mondays straight. For a stronger effect, you can fast for five years or until you get married. Preparation begins on Sunday: it is better to eat a light meal and preferably skip dinner. On Monday you should get up before sunrise, take a lukewarm shower. During the whole day, a strict fast just with the water or with one light meal is observed. It is favourable to recite the mantra to Shiva "Om Namah Shivaya" 108 times or as much as you like early in the morning. You can also meditate on the image of Shiva and Parvati, donate milk and fruits.

holiday.title: Eclipse Season
holiday.description:
Late summer brings an eclipse along the axis of the collective and the personal. Eclipse Season frees you from attachment to groups, ideologies, and social roles that no longer fit you. A cycle is ending in the realm of community life, groups, and sometimes friendship. Space opens up for what will align more closely with your calling and values. The universe offers a reminder: not every connection that once gave meaning has to last forever. Something is ready to be released.

How to navigate this period

Eclipse Season is the period between two eclipses, when karmic processes and subconscious patterns rise to the surface. It's a challenging yet very powerful time, carrying transformation and spiritual evolution. Events that happen during this period often change the course of life.

This period is well suited for:
– Meditation, silence practice, and observation.
– Letting go of what's ready to end: relationships, projects, roles, beliefs.
– Journaling, since the events and realizations of this period carry long-term meaning.
– Tracking dreams and intuitive signals — during Eclipse Season, they are especially informative.

It's best to avoid making major decisions, starting new projects, signing contracts, or having emotionally charged conversations. Try to shield yourself from a heavy flow of information, crowds, contact with difficult people, and negative content. This isn't a time for action, but for awareness. Everything that comes to light now will shape your future, so let the process unfold in its own way.
