holiday.title: Naga Panchami
holiday.description:
Naga Panchami is one of the most important Vedic holidays. It is dedicated to the Nagas or divine snakes. The celebration takes place on the fifth day of the waxing Moon in the month of Shravana.

In astrology, a snake is connected with two planets, Rahu and Ketu. Rahu symbolizes the snake’s head and sharp teeth which can punish and Ketu is the lower part of the body, hidden poison and transcendence. Engaging in a prayer on the day of Naga Panchami you can recharge with the strength and wisdom of Nagas, and also establish a balance between Rahu and Ketu.

In southern India, the holiday is held solemnly as snakes are treated with special respect and pride there. In all temples and outside you can find a variety of deities and images of the Nagas. People believe that any harm done to snakes will cause disasters and suffering.

During a week before the holiday, people catch cobras and place them in clay pots to release with songs and dances on the day of celebration. Also, they carry out the traditional rite of Abhishek — washing the deity with auspicious liquids, milk or juices. Some of the milk and treats used in the puja is taken home to treat all family members as a Prasāda (sacred food).

It is believed that meeting a snake on your way leads to great luck. For unmarried women, it is a sure sign to find marital happiness soon.

Naga Panchami is one of the best days for harmonizing Rahu and Ketu. For practice, find a habitat of safe snakes in advance or prepare figurines and an image of Nagas. Do not forget about the offerings: the Nagas love milk, white rice and milky sweets. After the practice, leave part of the Prasāda to snakes and take home the other one to treat your family. Alternatively, a day before the holiday, you can keep fast and complete it with the Prasāda.

Accompany the sacred process by reading mantras.

Navanaga Mantra is a mantra read before the puja that is dedicated to the nine main Nagas. The mantra invokes the snakes' power to succeed in any area.
ANANTAM VASUKI SESHAM PADMANABHAM CHA KAMBALAM
SHANKHAPALA DHRITARASTRAM TAKSHAKAM KALIYAM TATHA
ETHANI NAVA NAMAMI NAGANAAM CHA MAHATMANAM
SAYYAM KALE PATHE NITYAM PRATAH KALE VISHETATA
TASMAI VISHABHAYAM NASHI SARVATRA VIJAYE BHAVET

During the puja, mantra is repeated:
SARVA NAGAM PRIESTYAM MAYE KECHIT PRITHWI THALE
YE CHA HELIMARICHISTHA YENTARE DIVI SAMS TITHAH
YE NADISHU MAHA NAGA YE SARASVATI GAMINAH
YE CHA WAPI TADAGASH TESHU SARVESH WAI NAMAHA

The mantra is aimed at the satisfaction and glorification of the Deities.

After it, the Gayatri mantra should be repeated the maximum number of times.
NAG GAYATRI MANTRA
NAVA KULANAGAYA WIDMAHE
VISHADANTAYA DHIMAHI
TANNO SARPACH PRACHODAYAT

Another powerful mantra which power grows on Naga Panchami, is the Mahamrityunja Mantra. It cleanses the mind, eliminates the illusion and ignorance and helps to purify karma.
OM TRYAMBAKAM YAJAAMAHE
SUGANDHIM PUSHTI VARDHANAM
URVAARUKAMIVA BANDHANAN
MRITYOR MUKSHIYA MAAMRITAT

Remember that all rituals are aimed to protect you and your family. You save the family from curses, illnesses, failures and enemies, and of course restore harmony.

And remember this — like all snakes we have poison inside. Learn to control it and don’t let it destroy you from within.

According to the legend, during a difficult war, the king of heaven, Indra, was able to defeat a strong demon only after his wife tied a silk amulet on his wrist. This is how the main tradition of the holiday appeared: on this day, the sisters put on the sacred silk bandages called "rakha" on the right wrists of their brothers. They are decorated with multi-coloured threads, beads, precious stones, sequins which would give protection from evil forces. Girls also paint tikka on their brother's forehead - a red dot made out of special powder. Brothers then bliss their sisters, promising them protection and patronage and give them gifts as a sign of love and affection.

It is a favorite holiday for all Indian families that treasure family values. People put on national clothes, prepare a festive dinner and various sweets. Married girls who had to leave their home, return to their family for the day to congratulate the brothers.

It’s interesting to note that this holiday is not not only for blood brothers and sisters. Having tied a sacred bandage on a man's wrist, a woman can thereby recognize him as a sworn brother, asking him for protection and patronage. It is also a symbol of solidarity and unity of the entire Indian people.

holiday.title: The birth of Krishna
holiday.description:
Krishna Janmashtami (from Sanskrit Janma — birth, Ashtami — the eighth day) is one of the most significant Vedic holidays. It is believed that the Great Krishna was born about 5000 years ago at midnight on the eighth day of the waning moon in the month of Shravana in the city of Mathura. The ancient scriptures of the Bhagavad Gita state that the Supreme Personality of Godhead appears on Earth from time to time, when religion becomes weak and godlessness reigns, to free the righteous and punish sinners.

"When the time came for the appearance of Lord Krishna, all the constellations were in the most favorable position. At that moment, an atmosphere of peace and prosperity was established everywhere — in the east, in the west, in the south and in the north. Auspicious combinations of stars were visible in the sky, and on earth — in all cities and villages, in the pastures and in the thoughts of people — happiness reigned" (the book "Krishna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead", based on the scriptures of the Bhagavata Purana)

This day is widely celebrated throughout India, regardless of the religion of people. From morning till late night, festivals and theatrical performances are held for several days. People glorify God by dressing in bright clothes. Everyone brings offerings to the temples in the form of flowers, fruits, sweets and pray to the image of Krishna on the altar. Joy and happiness are felt everywhere.

It’s also a holiday for every family, which is celebrated as tenderly and warmly as Christmas among Western people. Until midnight, people keep a strict fast and then they sit down at a table full of traditional dishes and give out Prasada on the streets.

This is the most auspicious day to indulge in thoughts about Krishna, ask him for help, for guidance on the spiritual path. You can listen to lectures by spiritual mentors, read books and scriptures about his birth in the family of Devaki and her husband Vasudeva, childhood, the victory over demons who personify human vices. It is auspicious to listen and chant the mantras of Krishna HARE KRISHNA and VISHNU SAHASRANAM. It is believed that any wish made on this day reaches Krishna himself and will certainly come true.

Krishna embodies the supreme, absolute Truth. He protects good and pacifies evil, gives everyone what they deserve. Krishna Janmashtami has a special energy. Spending the day blissfully, you can clear your karma, improve your destiny and come closer to a happy life.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

holiday.title: International day of Beauty
holiday.description:
September 9th is traditionally celebrated as the Day of Beauty. The holiday was initiated by the International Committee of aesthetics and cosmetology of CIDESCO and has been celebrated annually since 1995. In a broad sense, beauty is in everything that exists in the Universe and implies a way of being, creation and to some extent, we can say that beauty is the meaning of the Universe.

In the Vedas, beauty is the synonym of flourishing that is life in its most vivid representation. Beauty is not about appearance, brightness or charisma. This is the energy that is revealed over time with proper care of the body and soul. The subtle energy of inner beauty increases with the years. By engaging in beauty, one not only affects one's appearance, but also expresses love for the world.

On this day for the disclosure of energy and preservation of natural beauty it is necessary to observe the five primary elements on which Vedic culture is built: Earth, Water, Fire, Air and Ether.

Earth symbolizes fragrance. Try to use aromatic compositions based on essential oils without alcohol content. Such spirits protect the aura and nourish the subtle body.

Water is responsible for the taste. To stay young and healthy, it is recommended to drink at least 1.5 liters of pure water per day. You can start your day with a glass of warm water. The Vedas mention that it is beneficial to drink flower teas and milk with spices. It is better not to abuse coffee and alcoholic drinks.

Fire includes elements of visual perception of beauty: clothing, jewellery and makeup. It opens a space for creativity: you can experiment, look for ways to express yourself through your appearance, reveal different facets of your personality. 

The air is responsible for tactile touch. It is favorable to regularly do self-massage, knead muscles and ligaments, gently remove clamps. You can turn to professional masseurs, try different types of massage. According to the Vedas, 1-2 times a week it is useful to rub warmed coconut or sesame oil into the skin or to do special oil massage "Abhyanga". 

The ether is responsible for sound. Chanting mantras, reading affirmations, saying prayers and listening to pleasant music has a harmonious effect. Try to keep track of what you listen to, with whom you communicate, what acoustic field you create around you. 

Through self-care and the beauty of our own image we can influence the world around us. Finding beauty and harmony every day in small details reflects favorably on external beauty and vice versa. Be beautiful at all levels!

Examples of beauty affirmations:

I am the embodiment of divine beauty and health.
My body is the perfect haven for my pure soul.
I am in harmony with the beauty of this world, I am a part of it.
I am the epitome of youth and beauty.

holiday.title: Mabon
holiday.description:
(NORTH HEMISPHERE)

Mabon is one of the celebrations of the magical annual cycle of eight seasonal festivals — Wheel of the Year. It’s also the second day of the year when the night is equal to the day.

It’s celebrated on the day of the Autumnal Equinox, and it’s the season of preparation for the coming winter months.
The name Mabon comes from Welsh mythology. Mabon ap Modron is a prominent figure from the myth of King Arthur, who represented male fertility and vitality.

Mabon holiday symbolizes:
— farewell to the past and liberation from all that is outdated;
— the time to honor deceased women of the Kin;
— the end of the agricultural year, period of harvesting and gathering of fruits.
The end of the harvesting season and last collections of vegetables, fruits, and crops were celebrated even before Christianity. On this day, Celtic sorcerers performed rituals for the abundance and sufficiency of food in the winter.

Mabona rituals are rituals of cleansing the space around you and bringing it into balance and harmony. During Mabon, it’s good to spend time outdoors, in the forest, collecting mushrooms, seeds and fallen leaves. Those can be used to decorate your home, prepare a festive dinner, or saved for winter rituals. Traditional food — cornbread, beans and zucchini.
During Mabon, it’s recommended to resolve old disputes, pay off debts or renew agreements. Reflect on the past year, get rid of the unnecessary, and appreciate and thank the necessary.

A simple ritual to perform during this time of Mabon is to write down all outdated attitudes and completed situations on a piece of paper and burn them with a candle. Or do the same in the forest — write what you want to say goodbye to on the autumn leaves and throw them into the fire. If the leaves have burnt, it means that the intention to purify will be fulfilled quickly. If they were blown away by the wind, a resolution might take more time to come.

Happy Mabon!

holiday.title: Pitru Paksha

Pitru Paksha (from Sanskrit "fortnight of the ancestors") is a period of 16 lunar days, from Mahalaya Purnima (full moon) to Mahalaya Amavasya (no moon) of the month of Bhadrapada. During these two weeks of the year, it is favorable to perform ancestral practices and rituals dedicated to the family and ancestors.

According to Hindu mythology, the souls of the three previous generations of ancestors do not go to heaven but are located in the Kingdom between heaven and earth Pitru Loke which is ruled by Yama, the God of death. Shraddha offerings are made for the ancestors who are in the Pitru Loka. In order for the ancestor's soul to enter heaven, the son of the deceased must make offerings during the Pitru Paksha period. In addition to offerings, sons pray for the souls of deceased relatives for fourteen days.

The Pitru Paksha period has very strong energy and all family practices performed at this time will have the strongest effect. During this period you can change the fate of your family and thus get rid of negative scenarios. It is a good time to establish relationships, try to communicate as much as possible with parents and relatives and sort out old grievances.

Try to accept those members of the family who are considered excluded from the family, about whom no one usually speaks (fathers that have abandoned their children, unborn children, etc.). Thus, you accept your family for what it is and gain greater power.

During this period you should practice meditation to restore connection and unity with the family, say prayers for the forgiveness and blessing of the family.

Honor your deceased ancestors in the way that is accepted in your family. These may be offerings, memorial services, lit candles, prayers and visits to graves. Create your family tree by asking your relatives about all the family members in detail. The family tree depicted on paper will help to strengthen the meditation on unity with the family. Mentally ask your ancestors for help and protection. You can ask for help in procreation, health, family happiness and help in business and blessings.

It is favorable during this period to make donations and help those in need. Also, during the Pitru Paksha period, it is important to share food as well as feed birds and stray animals. Through the food you give energy to your ancestors.

To strengthen the connection for the period of Pitru Paksha, you can partake in a fast, mentally passing all benefits from it on to your ancestors.

One of the most important days in the Pitru Paksha period is the last day (the 16th lunar day from the full moon) — Mahalaya Amavasya. On this day, the ancestors come to visit us and it is necessary to "feed" them.

The important thing to remember is that the period of veneration of ancestors is considered unfavorable when it comes to establishing new businesses, large purchases, beginnings and celebrations, all attention must be paid to your family.

Pitru Paksha is a period with the strongest ancestral energies. By honoring the ancestors and performing ancestral practices, everyone can establish a connection with the family and get rid of negative blocks, thereby making their lives, the lives of their loved ones and their children much happier and fulfilling.

holiday.title: World Vegetarian Day
holiday.description:
World Vegetarian Day is celebrated annually on the 1st of October. The holiday originated in North America in 1977 and a year later it already gained worldwide popularity. It’s celebrated throughout the whole month of October and is considered to be the month of vegetarian awareness.

Originally, vegetarianism came from cultures where Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism were common and has been practised for many millennia. In the ancient Indian Vedas, there is the concept of “Ahimsa" which means the rejection of violence in any of its manifestations. In Ancient Egypt refusal to eat or use any meat and animal skin products was also widespread as it was based on Egyptians’ belief in reincarnation. It is also a historical fact that Pythagoras himself was a proponent of plant food and taught his followers to live in harmony with nature and urged people to abandon cruelty towards animals.

The term “vegetarianism” appeared in the XIX century when this trend came to Europe from colonized countries such as India where it was popular among the local population. Until then the plant-based diet was better known as the Pythagoras’ diet.

Now vegetarianism is gaining popularity all over the world and, traditionally, in honour of this holiday, various events aimed at educating and familiarizing with the vegetarian lifestyle are organized during the month. They include master classes and free tastings of various dishes in restaurants, as well as lectures on aspects and transitions to vegetarianism, plastic waste and conscious consumption. Capital cities like London, Dublin and Barcelona hold weekend festivals from time to time, which prove to be very popular.

Undoubtedly, vegetable food carries more energy and is better absorbed in the body. But despite the popularity of this trend, it is important to remember that one shouldn’t force anything on themselves. All people are unique and not every human body can live a full life without meat and fish, it is also important to take into account the region of residence. Tune in to the wave of your body and be in harmony with it.

Guru is a manifestation of the Higher consciousness, the Absolute and dispels the darkness of ignorance, instils confidence in students and in their abilities. It is believed that there is no need to specifically look for a guru — when the student is ready, the teacher will appear in their life.

In Vedic astrology, planet Jupiter is responsible for teaching and transferring knowledge as it’s the planet of knowledge, education, spirituality and abundance. In order to harmonize Jupiter, it’s favourable to get involved with charitable deeds on Thursdays, especially beneficial would be donating to monasteries, children's and educational institutions. Also, to restore communication, respect and reverence for teachers you may listen to and read out loud Guru Mantra dedicated to the three Supreme Mentors — Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva:

holiday.title: Sharad Navaratri
holiday.description:
This is one of the most honoured Hindu festivals. The Navaratri holiday (from Sanskrit "Nava" meaning nine, "ratri" meaning night) is dedicated to the worship of the Mother Goddess. It lasts for nine days and nights and is celebrated four times a year where autumn’s celebration is marked to be the most important one.
Sharad Navaratri is dedicated to the worship of the Goddess Durga — the embodiment of the Divine Mother Shakti, the wife of Shiva. According to ancient scriptures, for nine days and nights, the Goddess was fighting with the demons and eventually won. Therefore, the celebration personifies the struggle with one's own inner demons and one’s victory. This sacred period is favourable for spiritual practices, prayers and self-improvement.
Every day is dedicated to one incarnation of Durga. In the mornings when services are held, the goddesses are presented with gifts and addressed with prayers. On the last day, festivals and celebrations are held.

1. Shailaputri is "Daughter of the Mountains'', the incarnation of Parvati — the wife of Shiva. Worshipping her harmonizes the Moon, helps to immerse in meditation and self-knowledge. Mantra: OM DEVI SHAYLAPUTRIYAI NAMAHA.
2. Brahmacharini is the incarnation of Parvati before marriage — Sati. People pray to her for the strength, perseverance, prosperity and harmonization of Mars. Mantra: OM DEVI BRAHMACARINYAY NAMAHA.
3. Chandragana — emitting light, embodying beauty and courage. Harmonizes Venus. Mantra: OM DEVI CHANDRAGHANTAYAY NAMAHA.
4. Kushmanda is the creative force of the Universe, worshipping her harmonizes the Sun. Mantra: OM DEVI KUSHMANDAYAI NAMAHA.
5. Skandamata is the mother of Skanda. The day is dedicated to the power and mothers’ sacrifices made in an effort to protect a child. Corrects the influence of Mercury. Mantra: OM DEVI SCANDAMATAAY NAMAHA.
6. Katyayani is the daughter of the sage Katya who has the power of the Three Gods, the personification of courage and firmness. Harmonizes Jupiter. Mantra: OM DEVI KATYANYAY NAMAHA.
7. Kalaratri is a ferocious, furious personification at the moment when the Goddess sacrificed her white skin to defeat demons. Prayers to her harmonize Saturn. Mantra: OM DEVI KALARATRIYAY NAMAHA.
8. Mahagauri is a symbol of mind and peace. Harmonizes Rahu. Mantra: OM DEVI MAHAGAURIYAI NAMAHA.
9. Siddhidatri is a special form of Lakshmi, possessing all the perfect talents and bestowing them. Harmonizes the influence of Ketu. Mantra: OM DEVI SIDDHIDATRIYAI NAMAHA.
May the Navaratri period bring you light and prosperity!

Vijayadashami is also the tenth day of Navaratri. During this time, harvesting season is in full swing and the Hindus ask for blessings for the upcoming harvest from the mother goddess Durga.
This day is charged with the victory of divine forces over the forces of evil. Outside of a religious context, one can celebrate the victory of the spirit over matter, the soul over the mind, emotions over the body.
Recommendations during Vijayadashami:
Decorate your home with yellow and red flowers. Create an atmosphere of abundance by arranging the table with fruits and sweets.
Observe a fast. Abstaining from meat, fish, eggs and alcohol is a good place to start.
Donate to a cause that you care about and the one that has your trust.
Make sure to avoid things that take away your life force: judgment, anger, lust, greed, envy, pride, insecurity.
On this day, the impact from visiting holy places, pilgrimage, prayers and reading the scriptures is greatly enhanced.

Practice austerity.
Make plans for the future. Create a bucket list.

holiday.title: Mercury Retrograde in Libra
holiday.description:
Libra is the sign of relationships, diplomacy, and the search for balance. Mercury here brings us back to old agreements and unfinished dialogues. What was left unresolved before now rises to the surface — and this is a chance to finally bring things to a close. Be mindful in business and personal negotiations, as well as financial decisions: words may land differently than intended. On the other hand, this period is well suited for reconciliation, for reconsidering the role another person plays in your life, and for restoring harmony where it has been disrupted.

holiday.title: Karva Chauth
holiday.description:
It is a traditional holiday of married women in the northern part of India. It is celebrated on the fourth day of the Waning Moon in the month of Kartika and usually falls on October. "Karva" is an earthen jug, and "Chauth" is the fourth day after the Full Moon. Since ancient times, women have kept a strict fast on this day and prayed for the health and well-being of their husbands. Legend says that once a woman named Karva saved her husband from death and was not afraid to resist the god of death Yama for the sake of her husband. In memory of her devotion and dedication, the Karva Chauth holiday was created.

The sacred meaning of fasting is that with her asceticism, a woman shows her husband deep love and devotion, a willingness to endure in any difficulties for him. In return, husbands on this day thank their wives, give them gifts and jewellery. Also, the holiday unites women, helps to find new friends which is especially important for those girls who had to move to a new place and leave their families after the wedding.

Fasting begins the night before with the appearance of the Moon in the sky and lasts until the next night. Women keep a strict dry fast without food and water but pregnant and weakened women can eat fruits, drink water and milk. Women get together, visit relatives and friends. Towards the evening, they paint their hands with henna, dress up in holiday saris and put on the best jewellery. Everyone attends the temple to do puja — prayer. The Karva jar is filled with food and sweets and presented to the altar as a sign of worship of the Moon.

When the Moon reappears in the sky, the fast ends. At this moment, the husband must be there. Traditions are that a woman comes out of the temple and looks at the Moon through a sieve first and then at the face of her husband. It is believed that with her gaze, she protects him from misfortune. He presents his wife with the first pieces of sweets and water.

The Karva Chauth holiday is designed to unite families, strengthen love and mutual understanding between spouses and encourage the prosperity of a man and the whole family. Unmarried girls can also fast on this day to strengthen the energy of the Moon and find a woman’s happiness.

holiday.title: Halloween
holiday.description:
The holiday is celebrated each year on October 31 in many countries around the world. The English word "Halloween" comes from All Hallows' Eve — the eve of All Saints' Day.

Roots of Halloween go back to the Celtic festival of Samhain. Inheriting its symbolism, Halloween has also acquired many traditions of its own. On the night from October 31 to November 1, children and adults dress up in costumes and go around the neighborhood, knocking on doors, asking for sweets with the phrase "Trick or treat". Since the 20th century, there has been a tradition of making lanterns out of a pumpkin with a face carved out — Jack-O'-Lantern, in honor of the old Irish legend about Jack the Smith, who tried to trick the devil. Witches and their faithful helpers, black cats, are considered symbols of the holiday. Houses are decorated with candles and lanterns and other appropriate attributes: cobwebs, figurines of bats and ghosts.

Halloween opens up opportunities to explore yourself and your hidden inner world. On this day, you can face your fears and observe what emotions and feelings rise up in you. You can watch scary movies and suddenly realize that this is an interesting way to release tension. You can dress up as a witch and discover the archetype of a priestess with secret knowledge. Or one may discover that making tea or mulled wine is like creating a healing drink, where one can put not only honey and cinnamon, but also an intention for fruition of dreams. You can get important answers by asking Tarot and Runes for clues.

Try to take every opportunity to step outside the box and explore new facets of yourself. 

Happy Halloween!

holiday.title: World Vegan Day
holiday.description:
The term veganism was coined by an English animal rights advocate Donald Watson on November 1st, 1944. He considered it inhumane not only to eat animal meat but also to keep them in captivity and exploit them for food. 

Therefore, the main idea of the Vegan Society founded by him was the rejection of all animal products: meat, fish, seafood, dairy products, eggs and honey. Vegans do not use leather, wool or fur products, and they fight against all animal cruelty. 

In honor of the 50th anniversary of the Vegan Society, an international holiday was established — World Vegan Day. It aims to draw people's attention to the problem of animal cruelty and cruelty towards nature. Vegans worldwide hold petitions and charity events to spread awareness about their lifestyle and enable as many people as possible to make an informed choice. They also raise the problem of ecology since animal agriculture is a serious source of greenhouse gas emissions and destroys the planet's ozone layer. 

Ideas of vegetarianism and veganism originate in ancient India and some Mediterranean countries. In Indian philosophy, the rejection of meat is associated with the image of the sacred cow and the idea of reincarnation. 

However, each of us comes into the world with a different body structure and level of health, different tasks and needs. Take care of yourself, be mindful and only follow what works best for you. So you can consciously choose your lifestyle and nutrition. 

If you do not feel you are ready to give up consumption of animal products but want to contribute to caring for the environment, you can take other important steps: for example, use cosmetics that are not tested on animals, choose sustainable leather and fur substitutes, and avoid visiting zoos, dolphinariums and circuses.

holiday.title: Diwali (Deepavali)
holiday.description:
Diwali, or Deepavali is from Sanskrit meaning "row or series of lights", is an ancient Hindu holiday symbolizing the victory of light over darkness and the beginning of a new cycle of life. The celebration falls between the end of the rainy season, the harvest period and the beginning of winter.

Diwali is also known as the festival of fire. Fire symbolizes the Divine principle in every person, their eternal soul, all the purest and most beautiful in them. The flame expels evil forces and evil spirits, cleans space and gives light.

The celebration lasts for five days, each dedicated to the praise of a specific deity. The third day falls on the New Moon when the main event takes place — the Festival of Lights. People gather for grand festivities, lighting fireworks as thousands of lights illuminate the night sky. This symbolizes the victory of light over darkness, good over evil, truth over falsehood. Music played on the streets, with fireworks going off and firecrackers exploding constantly.

The holiday is dedicated to the goddess of prosperity Lakshmi, the wife of the god Vishnu. People pray to images and statues of Lakshmi, make offerings of fruits, milk and sweets. Rangoli are painted on the floor and walls in front of each entrance door — it’s a colourful ritual ornamental prayers made of coloured sand and painted grains. It is believed that negative energy gets entangled in a complex pattern and does not enter the house.

In the honor of Lakshmi, lamps and candles are lit in houses as well as small outdoor fireplaces. Traditional burning oil lamps are called Dipa. According to legend, on a moonless night, they illuminated the path home to god Rama after defeating Ravana. Family members and close people give each other gifts and sweets, play outdoor games and gambling, do charity work, and women draw Mehendi on their hands.

In order to receive the grace of the goddess Lakshmi on this day, it is favourable to clean the house, decorate it with lights, lamps and flowers and also draw a rangoli pattern in front of the entrance. You can repeat or listen to the mantra OM HRIM SRI LAKSHMI BYO NAMAH. Honoring Lakshmi brings prosperity, love, joy, success and abundance.

holiday.title: Mercury Retrograde in Libra
holiday.description:
Libra is the sign of relationships, diplomacy, and the search for balance. Mercury here brings us back to old agreements and unfinished dialogues. What was left unresolved before now rises to the surface — and this is a chance to finally bring things to a close. Be mindful in business and personal negotiations, as well as financial decisions: words may land differently than intended. On the other hand, this period is well suited for reconciliation, for reconsidering the role another person plays in your life, and for restoring harmony where it has been disrupted.

How to navigate this period

Mercury governs the mind, intellect, speech, and communication, so during its retrograde, people find it harder to understand one another, draw the right conclusions, and think logically. Information is absorbed less easily, and mistakes, misunderstandings, delays, and breakdowns become more common. During Mercury retrograde, it's best to hold off on new ventures, major deals and purchases, lending money, and entering into agreements that can't be adjusted later. Double-check any important information once the retrograde ends.

But this period also carries strong potential for bringing order to your life:
— Finish what you've been putting off: unfinished courses, books, broken items, debts, unkept promises.
— Sort out your paperwork and let go of things you no longer need.
— Reconnect with old acquaintances: some connections are ready to be closed gracefully, others deserve to be strengthened.
— Write down the negative thoughts that keep running through your mind, and reframe them as positive affirmations.
— Jot down any unusual ideas, plans, or projects that come to you. Once the retrograde ends, you'll be able to evaluate them and start putting them into action.

Meditate more often to calm the mind and stay present. May this period unfold in harmony for you!

holiday.title: World Kindness Day
holiday.description:
World Kindness Day is celebrated on November 13th. This holiday was born in 1997 in Japan thanks to the volunteers of the "World movement for kindness". A year later the first conference of the movement was held and the holiday has become a good tradition in almost all countries of the world. The meaning of the movement and the holiday is to create a kinder and more sympathetic world and the symbol of the holiday is an open heart.

On the day of kindness people traditionally give flowers to people they meet. In Singapore, for example, they give gerberas and in Russia they even arrange flash mobs, forming a "ring of solidarity” by holding hands. Such seemingly simple actions help people to open up to each other, meet each other halfway and unite despite language and cultural differences.

Research by psychologists from different countries shows that people who perform good deeds, show mercy and concern for their neighbour, live a more fulfilling and harmonious life. They cope with stress more easily, get sick less and live longer. But it is important to understand that actions should be performed from the heart and not as a manifestation of kindness with selfish goals or “now I will do well and karma will reward me later on”.

And, as always, to see the bigger picture you have to start with essential — with yourself. Open your heart to the world, stop scolding yourself, tune in to the fact that everything around you is filled with kindness, love and participation and start exchanging positive energy with the world.

A simple sincere smile will cheer someone up; a stray dog that has not been petted for a long time is sometimes more happy to be petted than to eat; an old neighbour may find it difficult to go to the market for food, while you can easily grab some food for them while you shopping for yourself. Such actions do not take much time and effort but what wonderful feelings and fullness can be experienced by performing them can not be conveyed in words.

This day can be devoted to the practice of opening the heart chakra — Anahata. This chakra is associated with the green colour, so meditation with the Yam mantra can be combined with visualization of green rays of light coming from the heart area or visualization of the forest and the noise of leaves. Meditation is performed after Pranayama — full yogic breath.
Affirmations for repetition: “I love myself and accept myself as I am”, “I am open to love”, “I am loved“, “I forgive myself".

Let this day change your life and fill your daily life with good deeds.

holiday.title: International men's day
holiday.description:
This holiday is celebrated in many countries around the world on November 19th. Its goal is to highlight the problem of gender discrimination against men, gender inequality in many areas and the preservation of men's health. The organizers aim to show the importance of a man in building a family and raising children.

The masculine energy, led by the Sun, is oriented towards creation and is directed outward — towards achievements in the outer world. It's responsible for self-realization, the formation of individuality, purposefulness and achieving goals. The manifested solar energy gives inner freedom and helps to enter the state of the Creator of one's life.

In the modern world, many imposed stereotypes oppress male individuality and set strict limits:
— A man should not show emotions.
— Men don't cry.
— A man must be fond of sports, be aggressive and self-confident.

But every person, regardless of sex and gender, is unique and has the right to manifest in the sincere way. It's time to abandon artificial ideals and define what masculinity means and what traits are essential for a man.

A man can develop both materially and spiritually. Working on emotional intelligence, recognition and a healthy way of experiencing emotions is favorable. It brings inner balance and mental clarity. Yoga can become a helpful tool, as yoga has been a male practice since ancient times. Also, body-oriented therapy and breathing practices help eliminate body blockages that have been formed in boys since childhood due to many limitations.

Congratulate your loved ones today. You can make nice small gifts, show attention and care, and express what you especially appreciate about them verbally. May the male energy on Earth become even more manifested and harmonious today!

holiday.title: Ekadashi Fast
holiday.description:
This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: Thanksgiving
holiday.description:
Thanksgiving is a national holiday celebrated on various dates in the United States, Canada, Grenada, Saint Lucia and Liberia. Its roots go back to 1620 when the first settlers from England arrived on the shores of America. With the help of native Americans, they managed to grow crops on foreign rocky soil, which saved them from starvation. In gratitude to native Americans and God in 1621, they celebrated Thanksgiving for the first time.

This is one of the warmest family holidays. Traditionally, generations of the family gather around a festive table. Stuffed turkey with cranberry sauce, sweet potatoes, pumpkin pie and apple cider are usually served. Vegetarians and vegans can substitute turkey for other plant-based alternatives and vegetables.

At the festive table, everyone says words of gratitude for all the good things that happened to them during the year, as well as thanking family members, friends and Higher powers. People attend churches, pray and light candles. Charity events are held across the country, and hot food is distributed to the homeless and the poor.

Gratitude is the most fertile soil in which the seeds of any positive intentions grow. By filling our hearts with love and gratitude, we reach high vibrations, where there is no place for programs of hatred, competition and greed. In this state, we can create and become happier.

Even if this holiday is not traditional in your country, it's a wonderful opportunity to express gratitude. Say warm words of gratitude to your loved ones. Write a list of the things you are grateful for in life. It's an excellent time to start a gratitude journal. You can make donations and volunteer to help those in need.

May this day be filled with light and gratitude. Thank you!

holiday.title: World Compassion Day
holiday.description:
World Compassion Day has been celebrated on November 28th every year since 2012. The idea was suggested by the Indian journalist, public figure Prithish Nandi. The symbol of the day is a tree of compassion with birds sitting on its branches.

The idea of the holiday is based on the ancient Indian learning of Ahimsa. Its principles are embedded in many religions and spiritual learnings, including Buddhism.

Ahimsa is a philosophy of love and mercy, of causing no harm and suffering to any living being — not by word, nor deed, nor by thought. That is non-violence in any manifestation. The principles of Ahimsa concern both external intentions and internal attitudes of a heart.

The holiday calls to fight evil but at the same time not to succumb to hatred and revenge. The most important thing is to confront not the very people who create violence, but the sources of evil, its global causes. This can be done by understanding and following principles of humanity and personal responsibility for the fate of animals, nature, and other people. It is important to consciously exclude any violent attitudes and hostility.
On this day, charity events and fairs are held around the world to help animal shelters, adults and children in need. Anti-war rallies and performances are also made.

Compassion is the highest manifestation of love, the basis of harmony with yourself and the world. By emitting light and good deeds, you attract the favour of the universe and receive good in return. Remember that it is important to have compassion not only for the outside world but also for yourself. To do this, you can read or listen to the powerful mantra OM MANI PADME HUM which should be repeated 108 times. Turning to it, you pray for the good of all things, thereby improving your karma, saving the soul from an endless cycle of rebirth.

holiday.title: Ekadashi Fast
holiday.description:
This is the most auspicious day for observing a fast, purifying the spirit and body. The austerity on Ekadashi teaches self-control and abstention from momentary desires, improves karma, helps to detoxify the body and refresh the mind.

The fast consists of abstaining from grain and bean products and heavy, unhealthy food. Beginners may abstain from meat, fast on fruits, or only on water. Those who practice regularly may observe a dry fast — its effect will be the most powerful.

On the day before, it is not recommended to consume heavy food, and in the morning, it is best to rise with the sun, bathe, wear clean clothes, and mentally prepare for the fast.

The main thing on this day is to maintain pure thoughts, not to give in to anger, and to perform good deeds. It is auspicious to engage in spiritual practices, meditation, and prayer.

The next morning after Ekadashi, you may eat some fruits or grain products to gently break the fast.

VISHNU SAHASRANAMA MANTRA (the thousand names of Vishnu) is a very powerful mantra, especially during the Ekadashi period.

holiday.title: Winter and Summer Solstice
holiday.description:
This event is shown for both hemispheres. Scroll down to see how it's experienced where you are.

The Winter Solstice Day 

This day marks the shortest day and longest night of the year. Since ancient times, one has considered it the first step towards rebirth, starting a new life cycle, the path towards the sun and happiness. People greeted winter, built fire pits, partook in festive activities and rejoiced at the growing day and its victory over the dark, long night.

How to spend the day

Like all living things in nature, we get ready for rebirth and start accumulating creative energy. That is why it’s better to spend the day in a good mood, without quarrels, resentments and sadness. On this day, don’t limit yourself in terms of food — on the contrary, indulge yourself and enjoy your favorite dishes. The energy of this day strengthens your intention to let go of everything that has become obsolete, to cleanse your body and mind and renew. You can take a warm bath with sea salt and relax, imagining how water and salt take away all the problems and negativity. Spend the evening with your family or alone, engaging in spiritual practices, meditation, and favorite hobbies. 

Rituals

You can carry out some cleansing rituals to start the new year fresh — clean up, declutter, and sort things out. You can light incense and illuminate all the house corners with candles. On this day, it’s best to wake up at sunrise, take a shower and do spiritual practices. It can be yoga exercises like “Surya Namaskar” which is a Sun Salutation. It’s favorable to read or listen to mantras dedicated to the Sun, for example, OM HRAM HREEM HRAUM SAHA SURYAYA NAMAHA.

The Summer Solstice Day

Since ancient times this day has symbolized the onset of summer, the peak of thriving nature. It was a tradition to watch the sunrise together and then eat in celebration, take walks, swim, and make fires on this day.

How to spend the day

Try to surround yourself with the sun! In the morning, you can do exercises or yoga as well as practice “Surya Namaskar”, literally translated as Sun Salutations. If you put your breakfast in the sunlight, it will be charged with positive energy. Put on bright clothes and spend more time outside if you feel like it. This day is favorable for creativity, hobbies and communication with loved ones. 

Ritual

Light a candle. Get comfortable in a quiet place and engage in meditation to clear your thoughts. Think about everything you want to let go of in your life, and then imagine it’s burning with a candle’s flame. Thank the Universe for its lessons and open yourself up for happy changes and make a wish.

holiday.title: Christmas
holiday.description:
Christmas is a wonderful holiday that is associated with beautiful scents of cinnamon, cardamom, pine needles and fresh pastries. Time to make wishes and dream about the most sacred things. This day symbolizes the birth of Jesus Christ in Bethlehem.

The exact date of Christ's birth is unknown, so December 25 was chosen by the clergy in the IV century. This period also includes the Winter Solstice, the feast of the Sun birth, when the god of Kolyada appeared, so the church and pagan traditions are closely intertwined.

Unlike Catholics and Protestants, the Orthodox Church celebrates Christmas on January 7th. This is due to the differences in the Julian and Gregorian calendars but the essence of the holiday remains the same. Christmas has long-ceased to be a pure church custom; now it is celebrated throughout the world even by non-believers as a symbol of family unity and magic. 

Holiday traditions:
The month before Christmas is called Advent — this is the period of fasting, prayers, spiritual abstinence, charity and all events associated with Christmas. Four days before the holiday, children and adults traditionally take to the streets caroling, singing songs, receiving treats and gifts.

On Christmas Eve some people keep a strict fast. It ends with the appearance of the first star in the sky and then you can eat hearty porridge with honey. Christmas services are held at midnight, at dawn and in the afternoon.

It is customary to spend the holiday with the whole family in a decorated house and to prepare a lot of tasty dishes. The tradition of decorating the Christmas tree came from the Germanic peoples, for whom it was a symbol of life and fertility, a tree of paradise. The modern character of Santa Claus was based on traditions surrounding the historical Saint Nicholas and traditional pagan sacrifices degenerated into the custom of giving each other presents.

The holiday has clean bright energy, so on this day and especially at night, everyone can become a magician themselves so to speak. All rituals need to use lit candles as a symbol of the Bethlehem Star.

It is believed that at Christmas the angels descend to earth and fulfill all sincere, bright desires. Before going to bed you can think of your wishes or write them down and place that piece of paper by the windowsill.

holiday.title: New Year
holiday.description:
This bright fabulous holiday is celebrated in many countries around the globe and is associated with bliss, magic and happiness. It returns us to our childhood and allows us to believe in miracles once again.

New Year is not an astrological holiday as it is not connected with processes in the Universe. However, it has firmly entered modern life and our consciousness which means that it is a good reason to turn your life in the desired direction.

New Year's hustle and bustle can often get in a way of truly enjoying this fantastic holiday. Today, allow yourself to relax, leave the old year with all its negative aspects behind and enter the New Year updated and ready for change. Remember all the important moments of the past year, thank the Universe for its gifts and lessons.

Remember that especially during this holiday it’s favorable to take care of people and nature around. In the upcoming year, you can make a charitable contribution or give unnecessary things to those in need, so you will do good and make room for new things in your life.

May the coming year be filled with happiness and prosperity.
Happy New Year!
